q: A trendline with only one touch is…
opts: A guess — a wish, not a level
why: One touch is a guess, two touches draw a line, three touches make a level the market cares about.

q: In an uptrend, the trendline is drawn…
opts: Under the rising swing lows — the buyers' floor
why: An uptrend is higher highs and higher lows, so its line connects the lows — it is the buyers' floor. Never mix: a line touching both is a channel.

q: A wick pokes through the trendline but the candle closes back inside. This is…
opts: A fakeout — the close is the verdict
why: A break counts on the close, not the wick. A fakeout spikes through, fills the stacked orders, then closes back inside and reverses hard.

q: In an ascending channel, where is the defined edge to trade?
opts: The lower rail — buy the pullback, stop below, target the upper rail
why: The lower rail is the trading edge: pullback entry with a reaction candle, stop below the rail, target the upper rail. The middle is no-man's land.

q: An uptrend line broken from above changes its role to…
opts: Resistance — that is what the retest tests
why: A broken trendline flips roles: an uptrend line broken from above becomes resistance; a downtrend line broken from below becomes support. The retest tests that role change.
